package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	m := make(map[int]int)
	m[1] = 2
	fmt.Println(len(m))
	fmt.Println(m[1])
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	m := make(map[int]int, 8)
	m[1] = 1
	m[2] = 2
	m[3] = 3
	fmt.Println(len(m))
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	var m map[int]int
	delete(m, 1)
	fmt.Println(len(m))
}
What is the difference between var m map[int]int and m := map[int]int{}?
options: var is nil; {} is empty and not nil. Both have len 0

questions.text: What does writing to a nil map do?
options: It creates an empty map and stores the key

questions.text: Why use the comma-ok form v, ok := m[k]?
options: ok is the hash of the key
It is required to read any map
ok is false when the key is missing, even if the zero value was stored
ok is true only for string keys

questions.text: Does range over a map visit keys in a fixed order?
options: No. The order is not specified and may change

questions.text: What is n in make(map[K]V, n)?
options: A capacity hint for allocation, not a maximum length
A hard cap: the (n+1)th insert panics
The initial length, as in make([]T, n)
The number of buckets that can never grow

questions.text: What does a function receive when you pass a map?
options: A copy of every key and value
A copy of the map header that still points at the same table
Nothing: maps are passed by name
A pointer to the caller’s map variable

questions.text: Which types may be map keys?
What does delete(m, k) do if k is not in m?
options: It inserts k with the zero value

questions.text: What do you get when you read a missing key as v := m[k]?
options: The zero value of the value type
A compile error unless you use comma-ok

questions.text: Are len, range, and delete safe on a nil map?
options: Only len is safe; range and delete panic
Yes. len is 0, range does nothing, delete is a no-op

questions.text: What happens to len when you overwrite an existing key?
Can you compare two map values with m1 == m2?
options: No. A map is comparable only with nil

questions.text: var m map[int]int is nil.
m := map[int]int{} is nil.
Assigning to a nil map panics.
delete on a nil map panics.
for range over a nil map panics.
make(map[int]int, 4) rejects a fifth insert.
range visits map keys in sorted order.
The comparison m == nil is allowed.
A missing int key reads as 0.
Passing a map copies every key/value pair.
Writing the same key again increases len.
The ok in v, ok := m[k] is false when the key is missing.
What is the zero value of a map type?
How do you tell a stored zero value from a missing key?
questions.answer: Use the comma-ok form v, ok := m[k].

questions.text: What happens if you assign into a nil map?
Is the iteration order of a map specified?
What does n mean in make(map[K]V, n)?
questions.answer: An allocation hint, not a length cap.

questions.text: What is copied when you pass a map to a function?
questions.answer: The map header; the table is shared.

questions.text: What constraint do map keys have?
What does delete do for a key that is not present?
What is len of a nil map?
Name two ways to get an empty non-nil map.
questions.answer: make(map[K]V) or a composite literal map[K]V{}.

questions.text: What does ok mean in v, ok := m[k]?
questions.answer: Whether k is present in the map.
